headline: Tk 4,000cr deficit: Islami Bank faces severe cash crunch after board row
summary: The country's largest private bank has imposed withdrawal limits as Bangladesh Bank dissolves its board and injects Tk 2,500cr in emergency liquidity support.
details: Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC has plunged into a severe cash crunch within just 14 days, moving from a stable position to a deficit of approximately Tk 4,000 crore in its central bank account.

The crisis followed disruptions surrounding the appointment of a new chairman, leading to mounting withdrawal pressure from depositors. In response, the central bank dissolved the bank's entire board and appointed an administrator.

Acting Managing Director Md Altaf Hossain stated that customers are withdrawing an average of Tk 1,000 crore daily. To manage the pressure, the bank has officially imposed a Tk 50,000 cash withdrawal limit per customer at branches.
Some customers in Dhaka have reported that branches are allowing withdrawals of only Tk 10,000. The bank has also struggled to maintain its required cash reserve ratio (CRR) with the central bank.

To stabilize the situation, Bangladesh Bank has injected Tk 2,500 crore in special liquidity support. Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan confirmed the emergency funding to restore fund transfer and clearing services.
The liquidity damage was exacerbated by a drop in total deposits, which fell from Tk 1,84,382 crore on May 31 to Tk 1,80,141 crore by June 7.

The unrest began after the appointment of Md Khurshid Alam as chairman on May 24, which triggered protests from the Conscious Customers' Forum and demands for the reinstatement of former MD Omar Faruk Khan.
caption:

Acting Managing Director Md Altaf Hossain stated that customers are withdrawing an average of Tk 1,000 crore daily. To manage the pressure, the bank has officially imposed a Tk 50,000 cash withdrawal limit per customer at branches.

Some customers in Dhaka have reported that branches are allowing withdrawals of only Tk 10,000. The bank has also struggled to maintain its required cash reserve ratio (CRR) with the central bank.

To stabilize the situation, Bangladesh Bank has injected Tk 2,500 crore in special liquidity support. Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan confirmed the emergency funding to restore fund transfer and clearing services.

The liquidity damage was exacerbated by a drop in total deposits, which fell from Tk 1,84,382 crore on May 31 to Tk 1,80,141 crore by June 7.
